properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, ON THE TWO SETTLED HALVES. The third sub-question is SPLIT OUT to `dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams` (parked, trigger named) rather than left holding this one open.**

THE IDEA, Anthony's words 2026-08-08: *"the allocation of functions to systems/services should be done as late as possible (agreeing that doing it at genesis is too early). I feel like doing it at the last possible moment before functional allocation to system/service is the right call."* It answers a caution raised against `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph`, which proposed asking at GENESIS what quality attribute a system is for: the objection was that at genesis you frequently do not know yet, and premature commitment costs as much as late discovery. His resolution keeps the question and moves WHEN it is asked — to the moment allocation must actually be committed.

THE HOOK ALREADY EXISTS: `unallocated_capability` is already a detected gap, so "capabilities exist, bound to nothing" is visible from graph state alone — the same state-not-history discipline `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` commits to. Nothing new needs remembering.

**(a) PER-PROJECT OR PER-CAPABILITY — SETTLED 2026-08-08. PER-CAPABILITY SCOPE, PROJECT-LEVEL DEFAULT, RE-ASKED ONLY ON DIVERGENCE.** The schema already leans this way: DimensionAssessment attaches to ANY node, not to the Project, and a telemetry path and a config service in one system genuinely want different objectives. The recurrence worry — a mature design allocates continuously, so the moment repeats — is answered by machinery that already exists: an acknowledgement LAPSES when the shape it was accepted about changes, so the answer is recorded once and re-asked only when a new capability diverges. Recurring without being repetitive. ⚠️ Held most loosely of the three by the person who proposed it, and worth revisiting if the divergence test proves hard to state.

**(b) IS 100% ALLOCATION AGAINST 0% SEAMS AN INVERSION — MOVED OUT 2026-08-14 to `dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams`.** It is unanswerable from data the graph holds: 156 ALLOCATED_TO edges carry only `weight_basis`, nothing dates an allocation, and 1 of 320 ChangeEvents mentions one. Its trigger is "allocation timing becomes recordable at all". **Splitting it is the ruling: two settled halves should not read as undecided because a third is blocked on a substrate that does not exist.**

**(c) A DESIGN THAT NEVER REACHES THE MOMENT — CLOSED 2026-08-08**, answered by doctrine that already existed. `maturity_report` deliberately refuses to say where a design SHOULD be, and its own output says a demonstrator *"may sit here forever and be right"*. So never allocating is a **LEGITIMATE TERMINAL STATE**, not an error or a stalled process. The only thing any future prompt owes is to be acknowledgeable like every other gap — which every gap already is.

⚠️ **COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE THE RULING RATHER THAN ANSWERED BY IT, AND FLAGGED TO HIM BEFORE HE ACCEPTED:** the last-responsible-moment principle assumes deciding late costs less than deciding wrong, which holds only when deferral is free. Here it may not be — artifacts get written against an assumed structure long before anyone calls `allocate`. **If real files already embody a de facto allocation, then deferring the decision defers only the RECORD of it, and the graph arrives late to something the build already did.** That is the as-designed-versus-as-built gap `granularity_report` exists to surface, and it argues the trigger should watch **ARTIFACTS APPEARING** rather than the `allocate` call. Accepted with this open.
properties.name: DECIDED — allocation is deferred to the last responsible moment: per-capability scope with a project default, and never allocating is a legitimate terminal state
properties.rationale: Revised under revise-design with a snapshot taken while all three sub-questions still read open (epoch:allocation-subquestions-narrowed, seq 289), so the state before the narrowing survives. Status stays `proposed` deliberately: two sub-questions closing does not settle the parent, and flipping it would assert a decision Anthony has not made. The most valuable thing added is not either answer but the finding under (b) — that the agreed method could not be executed, and why. A parked question with a stated trigger is recognisable when someone walks past the answer months later; a parked question with none is indistinguishable from a forgotten one, which is a distinction reflow2 cannot currently draw at all (detect_defects reports parked decisions as `orphan_node`, info severity, and two of the four outstanding structural defects are exactly that).
